proposed_comments.title: Select the restore monitor after translating workspace coordinates
proposed_comments.body:
### Select the restore monitor after translating workspace coordinates

**Severity:** `high`

The earlier conversion helper chooses a monitor directly from `WINDOWPLACEMENT::rcNormalPosition`, but that rectangle is in workspace coordinates for ordinary top-level windows. A top or left taskbar can shift the rectangle across an adjacent monitor boundary, causing the restore preview or maximize operation to use the wrong monitor. Use a two-pass conversion: derive a tentative work-area offset, translate a reference rectangle, select the monitor again from that translated rectangle, and only then apply the final monitor's offset.

proposed_comments.title: Keep frame conversion off the low-level mouse-move hot path
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep frame conversion off the low-level mouse-move hot path

**Severity:** `high`

The earlier preview suggestion calls `GetWindowRect` and `DwmGetWindowAttribute` on every throttled low-level mouse move while the cursor remains over a snap target. `PrepareOverlayMetrics` already caches the invisible-frame margins at drag start and refreshes them after restore, so derive the preview's outer bounds from `g_overlayMarginL`, `g_overlayMarginT`, `g_overlayMarginR`, and `g_overlayMarginB` instead. This keeps the global hook responsive while preserving preview alignment.
